questions.prompt: Which action most clearly invalidates a comparison of two RL algorithms?
options: Picking each method's best checkpoint using the same episodes later used to report its score
Training both methods for exactly the same number of environment steps in each run
Reporting the interquartile mean as well as the plain mean of the returns of each method
Using the identical environment version and settings for both of the compared methods
questions.explanation: Selecting on the reported data inflates the result by roughly the expected maximum of the noise. The other choices are good practice.

questions.prompt: Per-seed standard deviation 10; you want a 95% confidence half-width of 2. How many seeds (use z = 1.96, round up)?
Returns of 5 seeds: 10, 12, 11, 13, 9. What is the standard error of the mean (n-1 denominator)? (three decimals)
Var of one seed's evaluation episodes is 400 (sigma_e = 20), the seed-to-seed variance is 100, S = 10 seeds, m = 25 episodes each. What is the variance of the grand mean? (two decimals)
You have enough budget for either 5 seeds x 200 episodes or 20 seeds x 50 episodes. Seed-to-seed variance is large compared with episode variance. Which is better and why?
options: 20 x 50: seed variance only shrinks with more seeds
Neither: the variance does not depend on either
They are equal because the total episodes are the same
questions.explanation: Var = sigma_s^2/S + sigma_e^2/(S m). The first term only falls with S, so more seeds win when sigma_s is large.

questions.prompt: A report pools 100 evaluation episodes from 5 seeds and gives a confidence interval from the sample standard deviation divided by sqrt(100). What is wrong and how do you fix it?
rubric: Episodes from the same seed are not independent: they share the seed's policy
The interval is too narrow: the effective sample is closer to 5 seeds
Fix: aggregate per seed first and compute/bootstrap the interval over seeds
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Write a predeclared evaluation protocol for comparing two RL methods in five lines or fewer.
rubric: Fixes training seeds and a disjoint evaluation seed set
Fixes steps, number of evaluation episodes, selection rule (final or validation-based) and statistic with interval
Includes a baseline and the same tuning budget for both methods
